401913646.summary: Gane's striking, reach advantage, and recent KO form support the consensus lean, but his age, two recent non-finishes, and Hokit's perfect record with five straight KOs create enough uncertainty that the -190 price is not a parlay-heavy favourite.
reasons: Gane's 81-inch reach and striker profile give him range control against Hokit's 73.5-inch frame
Gane's last two wins include a KO over Pereira (R2) and 7 KOs in 14 wins; KO method aligns with his record
Hokit is 10-0 with five straight wins and six KOs in 10 fights, but unproven against elite competition at this level
Gane is 36 and shows recent fatigue (draw with Aspinall, split decision over Volkov); Hokit brings youth and momentum

401913647.summary: Thompson's technical striking and decision-heavy record align with the consensus, but age, inactivity, and recent losses create enough uncertainty that the -155 price is fair rather than exploitable.
reasons: Thompson's 8 decision wins versus only 2 KO losses and 1 submission loss fit a decision outcome, matching the consensus method call at 41.4%
At 43 with 488 days away and three straight losses (two brutal finishes), Thompson is likely declined enough that Radtke's power and recent activity (215 days,
The moneyline price of -155 fairly reflects Thompson's skill edge but doesn't compensate enough for age, recency, and finish vulnerability in a parlay context

401922638.summary: Harrison's submission prowess and recent form edge a vulnerable Nunes, but at -170 the favorite carries finish risk that makes parlay inclusion risky.
reasons: Harrison is 8-0 by submission in her wins; Nunes has been submitted twice recently, including by the same opponent Harrison just beat
Nunes is 38 with 1251 days away; Harrison is 36 with recent activity and momentum, having submitted three straight opponents
Capper lean on Nunes (54%, strength 5.4) contradicts the price; -170 overvalues a striker past her prime against an elite judo practitioner, especially when KO

401922639.summary: Borralho's recent decision wins and technical wrestling favor him over Belgaroui's hot striking streak, but the matchup is competitive and the moneyline pricing is tight.
reasons: Borralho has won his last three fights all by decision, showing consistent control and grappling in recent form against quality opposition
Belgaroui is 4-for-3 in KOs over his last five wins but faces a 6'1" southpaw with superior reach and mixed martial arts depth at Fighting Nerds
The -150 moneyline does not offer enough value given the consensus lean to Belgaroui and his recent momentum; the method call to decision aligns with Borralho's

401922640.summary: Medić's recent explosive form and knockout power give him the edge, but Holland's reach and decision-heavy record create enough uncertainty to reject parlay duty at -150.
reasons: Medić is 3-0 with three consecutive R1 KOs against solid competition (Salikhov, Neal, Rodriguez); Holland's last five show losses to decision specialists at wel
Holland's 81" reach gives positional advantage, but his decision-heavy record (6 dec wins, 9 dec losses) suggests he struggles to finish high-level opposition
Medić's finish rate is 87.5% (14 finishes in 17 wins) versus Holland's 74.2% (17 finishes in 23 wins); Medić's KO rate at welterweight is elite
The -150 price is reasonable but not steep enough for a 3-round fight where Holland's length and volume could steal rounds on the scorecards

401922641.summary: Hasan's perfect record, recent knockout streak, and significant physical advantages support the consensus pick, but the -950 line is overpriced for a flyweight with limited UFC sample size.
reasons: Hasan is 10-0 with 8 KOs; Gurule is 1-3 in last four fights with submission loss to Tsuruya 167 days ago
Hasan's reach advantage of 6 inches and switch stance versatility favor his striking-heavy KO method
Consensus KO call (98.5%) aligns with Hasan's 80% finish rate, but -950 moneyline is steep for flyweight matchup with limited elite competition for Hasan

401922642.summary: Dober's recent finish streak and significant experience edge outweigh Duncan's perfect recent record, but the matchup lacks clear conviction and the price requires justified confidence.
reasons: Dober has won his last two by finish (KO R2, KO R3) with strong KO finishing rate (17 wins by KO) versus Duncan's one KO loss in 18 fights suggesting durability
Duncan's perfect last five masks recent submission loss to Moicano; Dober's wrestling pedigree and submission wins (5) provide multiple paths to victory
Capper consensus leans Duncan but at only 6.2/10 strength with a lean tag, not conviction; the +155 price offers better value than the -172 favorite
Age and mileage concern: Dober at 38 with 44 total fights vs Duncan at 33 with 18 fights; Dober's WWLLL last five shows inconsistency on the come-down

401922643.summary: Miller's submission prowess and experience edge a chinny McKinney despite recent inactivity, but the matchup is close and the price doesn't compensate for the risk.
reasons: Miller's 22 submission wins dwarf McKinney's 9 and align with his wrestling base; McKinney has lost three of last five and two by finish
McKinney's recent KO loss to King Green and submission loss to Duncan suggest vulnerability to the exact tools Miller deploys
Miller at +180 offers modest value for a 43-year-old, but his submission wins (10 of last 10) vs McKinney's mixed offense justify the underdog price more than c
187 days away and age 43 are real concerns; McKinney's -215 price doesn't adequately reflect his finishing losses and chinny record in a grappler's fight

401922645.summary: Mesquita's perfect record, submission mastery, and stylistic advantages over a declining Chiasson warrant backing her, but the -250 price and submission-heavy method call create modest value concerns for parlays.
reasons: Mesquita undefeated 8-0 with 6 submission wins shows elite grappling; Chiasson's last five is 2-3 with three straight decision losses suggesting defensive strug
Chiasson at 35 with 257 days layoff faces a fresher, younger (also 35 but with shorter reach disadvantage) opponent riding momentum; recent losses all go distan
Mesquita's submission win rate of 75 percent and grappling pedigree from American Top Team align perfectly with capper consensus call, justifying the strong met
Minus-250 reflects Mesquita's clear edge but leaves little margin; submission finish risk is real and prices in most of the edge, making moneyline a weaker parl

401931773.summary: Donte Johnson is undefeated against a fighter in decline, but the -170 price overvalues him given Almeida's power and KO record.
reasons: Johnson's 9-0 record with 7 KOs vs Almeida's 7-3 with recent R1 KO loss shows clear quality gap
Almeida is 38 with LLWWL trend; Johnson is 27 and 5-0 in last five with no losses
Johnson's southpaw stance and reach parity (both 74 inches) suit his style against the taller Orthodox fighter
Johnson has finished 8 of 9 opponents; the -170 moneyline undercompensates for this finish rate and undefeated status

401931774.summary: Costa's recent form, size advantage, and finish rate justify consensus backing, but the -375 price is steep for a three-round lightweight fight with real KO risk for the favorite.
reasons: Costa is 4-1 in last five with three straight wins; Gordon is 1-4 in last five with recent losses to quality opposition
Costa owns 3-inch reach advantage and southpaw angle against an aging, smaller striker vulnerable to leg kicks and distance control
KO finish in 72.9% of method calls aligns with Costa's 9 KO wins and Gordon's 5 KO losses, but three-round format and -375 price limit parlay value

401932013.summary: Sanches' perfect recent form and heavy KO rate align with the capper consensus backing Elder by decision, creating conflicting signals that warrant caution on either side as a parlay piece.
reasons: Sanches is 11-1 with 8 KOs in 11 wins and 3 straight first-round finishes; Elder's recent wins lean toward decision (2 of last 3), not finishing
Capper consensus backs Elder by decision at 67.9% but the moneyline is nearly even money, suggesting the market disagrees with a strong lean
Elder's 565-day layoff is significant and his record shows he loses when pressed (WWWLL in last five); Sanches' youth, reach advantage, and aggressive finishing

401933936.summary: Diaz's dominant recent form, youth advantage, reach edge, and perfect activity level against a fading veteran make him the clear pick, but his lone loss and 180-day layoff prevent maximum confidence.
reasons: Diaz is 5-0 in last five with KO and submission wins mixed in; Alatengheili is 3-2 with aging profile and split decision struggles
Diaz at 28 with 69.5 inch reach versus Alatengheili at 34 with 66 inch reach gives significant physical advantages
Alatengheili's 47 days of recent activity is encouraging but his record shows decisioning tendency (10 of 19 wins) against Diaz's finish rate (8 of 16)
Diaz's only loss came by decision five years into his career suggesting durability, but 180-day layoff introduces modest risk to confidence level
